# OPTIMA CARE HEALTH INSURANCE POLICY - POLICY WORDING

**Product Name:** Optima Care Comprehensive Health Insurance  
**Product UIN:** IRDAI/HLT/OC/P-H/V.1/2024-25  
**Regulating Authority:** Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)  
**Document Type:** Standard Retail Health Insurance Contract Terms and Conditions  

---

## SECTION 1: DEFINITIONS AND INTERPRETATIONS

### Clause 1.1: Accident
An accident means a sudden, unforeseen, and involuntary event caused by external, violent, and visible means.

### Clause 1.2: Admission
Admission means the formal entry and registration of the Insured Person into a registered Hospital for medically necessary treatment of an Illness or Injury.

### Clause 1.3: AYUSH Treatment
AYUSH Treatment refers to medical and/or hospitalization treatments given under Ayurveda, Yoga and Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha, and Homeopathy systems in a government hospital or recognized institute.

### Clause 1.4: Cashless Facility
Cashless Facility means a facility extended by the Insurer to the Insured where the medical expenses incurred by the Insured at a Network Hospital are directly settled by the Insurer to the Hospital, subject to policy terms and agreed tariff.

### Clause 1.5: Co-payment
Co-payment means a cost-sharing requirement under this health insurance policy that provides that the Policyholder/Insured will bear a specified percentage of the admissible claim amount. A Co-payment does not reduce the Sum Insured.

### Clause 1.6: Day Care Treatment
Day Care Treatment refers to medical treatment and/or surgical procedures undertaken under general or local anesthesia in a hospital/daycare center in less than 24 hours of admission because of technological advancements, which would otherwise have required hospitalization of more than 24 hours.

### Clause 1.7: Deductible
Deductible means a cost-sharing requirement that provides that the Insurer will not be liable for a specified rupee amount of the covered expenses, which will first be borne by the Insured Person before benefits become payable by the Insurer. A deductible does not reduce the Sum Insured.

### Clause 1.8: Domiciliary Hospitalization
Domiciliary Hospitalization means medical treatment for an illness/disease/injury which in the normal course would require care and treatment at a hospital but is actually taken while confined at home under specific medical conditions where the patient cannot be moved or hospital beds are unavailable.

### Clause 1.9: Grace Period
Grace Period means the specified period of 30 days immediately following the premium due date during which a payment can be made to renew or continue a policy in force without loss of continuity benefits such as waiting periods.

### Clause 1.10: Hospital
A Hospital means any institution established for in-patient care and day care treatment of illness and/or injuries and which has been registered as a hospital with local authorities under Clinical Establishments Act and complies with minimum bed criteria (at least 15 beds in towns with population > 10 lakhs, 10 beds in all other towns).

### Clause 1.11: Illness
Illness means a sickness or a disease or pathological condition leading to impairment of normal physiological function which manifests itself during the Policy Period and requires medical treatment.

### Clause 1.12: Injury
Injury means accidental physical bodily harm solely and directly caused by external, violent, visible, and evident means which is verified and certified by a registered Medical Practitioner.

### Clause 1.13: Inpatient Hospitalization
Inpatient Hospitalization means admission in a Hospital for a minimum period of 24 consecutive hours for Medically Necessary Treatment.

### Clause 1.14: Intensive Care Unit (ICU)
Intensive Care Unit means an identified section, ward, or wing of a hospital which is specially equipped with monitoring and life support systems and staffed with dedicated medical personnel for critically ill patients.

### Clause 1.15: Medically Necessary Treatment
Medically Necessary Treatment means any treatment, test, medication, or stay in hospital which is required for the medical management of illness or injury, conforms to standard medical practice, and is not solely for the convenience of the patient or doctor.

### Clause 1.16: Network Hospital
Network Hospital means hospitals, health care providers, or clinics enlisted by an Insurer or by a Third Party Administrator (TPA) to provide medical services to an Insured on a Cashless basis. ### Clause 1.17: Non-Network Hospital
Non-Network Hospital means any registered hospital or medical facility that is not part of the network of the Insurer or TPA.

### Clause 1.18: Pre-Existing Disease (PED)
Pre-Existing Disease means any condition, ailment, injury, or disease that is diagnosed by a physician within 36 months prior to the effective date of the policy issued by the Insurer or for which medical advice or treatment was recommended or received within 36 months prior to policy inception.

### Clause 1.19: Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses
Pre-Hospitalization Medical Expenses means medical expenses incurred immediately before the Insured Person is hospitalized, provided that such expenses are incurred for the same condition for which hospitalization occurred, up to a maximum period of 60 days. ### Clause 1.20: Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses
Post-Hospitalization Medical Expenses means medical expenses incurred immediately after the Insured Person is discharged from the hospital, provided that such expenses are incurred for the same condition for which hospitalization occurred, up to a maximum period of 180 days.

### Clause 1.21: Reasonable and Customary Charges
Reasonable and Customary Charges means the charges for services or supplies which are standard and customary in the geographic area where the treatment is provided for similar illness or injury.

### Clause 1.22: Room Rent Limit
Room Rent Limit means the maximum daily amount covered by the Insurer towards room and boarding charges during inpatient hospitalization. Under Plan A, Room Rent is capped at 1% of Sum Insured per day. Under Plan B (Optima Super), Single Private Air Conditioned room is allowed with No Room Rent Capping.

### Clause 1.23: Sum Insured
Sum Insured means the pre-agreed maximum liability of the Insurer under this policy as specified in the Policy Schedule for any one policy year.

### Clause 1.24: Surgery or Surgical Procedure
Surgery means manual and/or operative procedure for correction of deformities, repair of injuries, or relief of suffering, performed by a qualified surgeon in an operating theater.

---

## SECTION 2: BASE COVERAGE BENEFITS

### Clause 2.1: Inpatient Hospitalization Expenses
The Insurer will cover medical expenses incurred for Inpatient Hospitalization exceeding 24 hours, including room boarding and nursing expenses, Intensive Care Unit (ICU) charges, fees of Medical Practitioner, Surgeon, Anesthetist, and Consultant, and charges for anesthesia, blood, oxygen, operation theater, surgical appliances, and diagnostic tests. ### Clause 2.2: Intensive Care Unit (ICU) Coverage
ICU charges are covered up to actual expenses under Plan B. Under Plan A, ICU coverage is capped at 2% of the Sum Insured per day.
Pro-rata proportion deductions will apply to associate medical expenses if room rent exceeding eligibility is selected.

### Clause 2.3: Pre-Hospitalization Coverage
Pre-hospitalization medical expenses are reimbursed up to 60 days prior to the date of admission, provided the inpatient hospitalization claim is admissible under Clause 2.1. ### Clause 2.4: Post-Hospitalization Coverage
Post-hospitalization medical expenses are reimbursed up to 180 days following the date of discharge from the hospital, provided the primary hospitalization claim is admissible. ### Clause 2.5: Day Care Procedures
Medical expenses incurred for all Day Care Procedures specified in Annexure I (over 500 procedures) are covered up to the Sum Insured, even though hospitalization is less than 24 hours, provided modern technological advancement necessitated shorter stay.
Outpatient consultations are not covered under this clause.

### Clause 2.6: Domiciliary Hospitalization Benefit
Domiciliary hospitalization is covered up to a maximum of 10% of the Sum Insured subject to a maximum of ₹50,000 per policy year, provided medical treatment continues for at least 3 consecutive days and the condition fulfills the definition under Clause 1.8.
Bronchitis, Asthma, Cough and Cold, and Diarrhea are excluded from Domiciliary benefits.

### Clause 2.7: Road Ambulance Cover
The policy covers road ambulance expenses incurred for transfer to the nearest hospital with adequate medical facilities, subject to a limit of ₹2,500 per hospitalization and a maximum of ₹5,000 per policy year.

### Clause 2.8: AYUSH Inpatient Treatment
Inpatient treatment taken under recognized AYUSH systems in a government AYUSH hospital or accredited institute is covered up to 100% of the Sum Insured without sub-limits, provided treatment is for an illness that otherwise qualifies for inpatient hospitalization.

### Clause 2.9: Organ Donor Expenses
Medical expenses incurred for in-patient hospitalization of an organ donor harvesting organ for the Insured Person are covered up to the Sum Insured, provided the organ is donated in compliance with Transplantation of Human Organs Act, 1994.
Screening expenses of donors are excluded.

### Clause 2.10: Cumulative Bonus (No Claim Bonus)
For every claim-free policy year, the Sum Insured shall be increased by 10% up to a maximum of 100% of the basic Sum Insured, provided the policy is renewed without any break. In the event of a claim, the accumulated bonus is reduced by 10% at renewal, but the base Sum Insured remains untouched. ### Clause 2.11: Restoration of Sum Insured
If the base Sum Insured and Cumulative Bonus are exhausted during the policy year due to claims paid, a 100% restoration of the base Sum Insured will be triggered automatically once per policy year for unrelated illnesses or injuries. Restoration cannot be utilized for the same illness for which a claim was paid within the same year.

---

## SECTION 3: WAITING PERIODS

### Clause 3.1: Initial Waiting Period (30 Days)
A waiting period of 30 days from the inception date of the policy applies to all claims, except accidental bodily injury.

Any illness diagnosed or manifesting during the first 30 days of coverage is permanently excluded from coverage under this policy. ### Clause 3.2: Specific Disease Waiting Period (24 Months)
A mandatory waiting period of 24 consecutive months of continuous coverage applies to the following listed conditions: Benign prostatic hypertrophy, Hernia, Hydrocele, Fistula and Fissure in ano, Piles, Sinusitis, Tonsillitis, Gall bladder stones, Renal calculi, Cataract, Hysterectomy for non-malignant conditions, Joint replacement surgeries unless due to accident, Osteoarthritis, and Spinal disc disorders. ### Clause 3.3: Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period (36 Months)
Medical expenses directly or indirectly related to any Pre-Existing Disease (PED) as defined under Clause 1.18 will not be covered until 36 months of continuous coverage have elapsed since the inception of the first policy with the Insurer.
If porting from another insurer, continuity benefit on the elapsed waiting period is credited as per IRDAI portability guidelines.

### Clause 3.4: Moratorium Period (60 Months)
After 60 continuous months of coverage under this policy, no claim shall be contestable by the Insurer on grounds of misrepresentation or non-disclosure of health conditions, except in instances of proven fraud.

---

## SECTION 4: DEDUCTIBLES, CO-PAYMENTS, AND LIMITS

### Clause 4.1: Standard Deductible Option
Where the policyholder opts for a Voluntary Deductible of ₹10,000 or ₹25,000 to reduce annual premium, the Insured must bear the selected deductible amount on aggregate admissible claims during each policy year before the Insurer pays any claim benefit.

### Clause 4.2: Senior Citizen Co-payment
A compulsory co-payment of 10% applies to all admissible claims if the Insured Person enters the policy at or after age 61.
The 10% co-payment is deducted from the net admissible claim after applying deductibles.

### Clause 4.3: Cataract Sub-limit
Coverage for Cataract surgery is limited to a maximum of ₹40,000 per eye under Plan A, and ₹60,000 per eye under Plan B, inclusive of lens costs and surgeon fees. ### Clause 4.4: Modern Treatment Methods Sub-limits
Modern treatments such as Robotic Surgeries, Oral Chemotherapy, Immunotherapy, and Stem Cell Therapy are covered up to 50% of the Sum Insured or ₹5,00,000, whichever is lower.

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL EXCLUSIONS

### Clause 5.1: Investigation and Evaluation Only
Expenses related to admission primarily for diagnostic, X-ray, or laboratory examinations with no active medical or surgical treatment are excluded. ### Clause 5.2: Rest Cure, Rehabilitation, and Respite Care
Expenses related to any admission primarily for bed rest, convalescence, rehabilitation, or nursing care at home or health resort are excluded.

### Clause 5.3: Obesity and Weight Control
Medical expenses for surgical or medical treatment of obesity or weight reduction are excluded unless BMI is greater than 40 and accompanied by life-threatening comorbidities as certified by a specialist. ### Clause 5.4: Cosmetic or Plastic Surgery
Expenses for cosmetic or aesthetic treatments, facelifts, or plastic surgeries are excluded unless necessitated by accidental injury, burns, or cancer reconstruction. ### Clause 5.5: Hazardous and Adventure Sports
Treatment expenses arising from participation as a professional in hazardous or adventure sports such as skydiving, motor racing, scuba diving, and mountaineering are excluded.

### Clause 5.6: Breach of Law
Expenses incurred for treatment directly caused by or arising from the Insured Person committing or attempting to commit an intentional breach of law with criminal intent. ### Clause 5.7: Substance Abuse and Intoxication
Expenses incurred for treatment directly or indirectly attributable to alcohol abuse, drug abuse, or use of intoxicating substances without prescription are excluded. ### Clause 5.8: Unproven Treatments and Experimental Therapies
Expenses for treatments, procedures, or medicines that are not recognized by standard medical boards or that are undergoing clinical trials are excluded.

### Clause 5.9: Maternity and Pregnancy Expenses
Medical expenses related to pregnancy, childbirth, caesarean section, abortion, or miscarriage are excluded, except ectopic pregnancy diagnosed by clinical ultrasound.

### Clause 5.10: Dental Treatment
Dental treatment or surgery of any kind is excluded unless requiring hospitalization following an accidental bodily injury.

---

## SECTION 6: CLAIMS PROCEDURE AND DOCUMENTATION

### Clause 6.1: Intimation of Cashless Claim
For planned hospitalization at a Network Hospital, pre-authorization must be submitted at least 48 hours prior to admission. In emergency hospitalization, claim intimation must be given within 24 hours of hospital admission. ### Clause 6.2: Intimation of Reimbursement Claim
For treatment at a Non-Network Hospital, written intimation of claim must be submitted to the Insurer or TPA within 48 hours of admission or prior to discharge, whichever is earlier. ### Clause 6.3: Claim Submission Deadline
All original bills, receipts, discharge summary, diagnostic reports, and medical prescriptions must be submitted to the Insurer within 30 days from the date of discharge from the hospital. ### Clause 6.4: Post-Hospitalization Claim Submission
Bills and receipts for post-hospitalization medical expenses covered under Clause 2.4 must be submitted within 30 days of completion of the 180-day post-hospitalization period. ### Clause 6.5: Required Claim Documents
A valid reimbursement claim dossier must include: Completed signed Claim Form Part A and B, Original Discharge Summary, Original Final Hospital Bill with itemized break-up, Original Payment Receipts, Pharmacy bills with supporting prescriptions, Doctor consultation sheets, and KYC documents for claims above ₹1,00,000.

### Clause 6.6: Claim Settlement Timelines
The Insurer shall settle or reject a claim within 30 days from the date of receipt of the last necessary document.
In case of delay, the Insurer is liable to pay interest at 2% above the bank rate as mandated by IRDAI.

# IRDAI CONSUMER EDUCATION AND INSURANCE CLAIMS FAQ COLLECTION

**Source:** IRDAI Consumer Education Portal & Grievance Guidelines  
**Domain:** Public Policyholder Assistance and Regulatory Standards  

---

## SECTION 11: HEALTH INSURANCE CONSUMER CLAIMS FAQS

### Clause 11.1: Cashless Claim Authorization Process
Under cashless hospitalization, the network hospital sends a pre-authorization request to the TPA or insurer.
The insurer must issue an initial approval or query within 1 hour of receiving complete medical details.

### Clause 11.2: Treatment in Non-Network Hospital
If an insured is admitted to a non-network hospital, the expenses must first be paid out-of-pocket by the policyholder and subsequently claimed through reimbursement within 30 days of discharge.

### Clause 11.3: Grace Period Continuity Benefits
If premium is paid within the 30-day grace period, all accrued benefits including waiting period credits for pre-existing diseases and cumulative bonuses are fully preserved without any penalty.

### Clause 11.4: Pre-Existing Disease Disclosure Norms
Failure to disclose pre-existing diseases at the time of policy proposal permits the insurer to reject claims arising within the first 60 months of policy inception on grounds of non-disclosure.

### Clause 11.5: Free-Look Cancellation Refund Deductions
When a policyholder cancels a policy during the 15-day free-look period, the insurer refunds the premium after deducting proportionate risk premium, medical examination costs, and stamp duty.

### Clause 11.6: Deductible vs Co-Payment Distinction
A deductible is a fixed rupee amount (e.g., ₹10,000) borne first by the insured per policy year. A co-payment is a fixed percentage (e.g., 10%) shared on every admissible claim amount.

### Clause 11.7: Day Care Procedures Hospitalization Criteria
Day care procedures do not require 24 hours of hospital confinement if advanced medical technology enables discharge within 24 hours in a registered daycare surgical facility.

### Clause 11.8: AYUSH Hospitalization Recognition
AYUSH treatments are admissible only if taken in a recognized government AYUSH hospital or an accredited teaching hospital under the Clinical Establishments Act.

### Clause 11.9: Pre-Hospitalization Diagnostic Tests Coverage
Diagnostic tests (such as MRI, CT scans, blood work) conducted within 60 days before hospital admission are reimbursable if directly related to the inpatient hospitalization condition.

### Clause 11.10: Post-Hospitalization Follow-up Pharmacy Bills
Pharmacy bills and follow-up consultation fees incurred within 180 days post-discharge are payable provided prescriptions from the treating medical practitioner are attached.

---

## SECTION 12: MOTOR INSURANCE CONSUMER CLAIMS FAQS

### Clause 12.1: Compulsory Deductible Engine Thresholds
Under Indian Motor Tariff regulations, private cars with engine capacity up to 1,500 cc carry a compulsory deductible of ₹1,000; cars exceeding 1,500 cc carry a compulsory deductible of ₹2,000.

### Clause 12.2: Mandatory FIR for Vehicle Theft
In the event of motor vehicle theft, immediate registration of a First Information Report (FIR) with the police is compulsory.
An insurance claim cannot be settled without an untraced report.

### Clause 12.3: Zero Depreciation Add-on Validity
A Zero Depreciation (bumper-to-bumper) add-on waives depreciation deductions on plastic, rubber, metal, and glass parts, but is generally available only for vehicles up to 5 years of age.

### Clause 12.4: Third Party Property Damage Statutory Limit
The statutory liability for third-party property damage under the Motor Vehicles Act is capped at ₹7,50,000 per accident. Unlimited liability applies only to third-party death or bodily injury.

### Clause 12.5: Transfer of No Claim Bonus to Replacement Car
When a car owner sells their vehicle, the earned No Claim Bonus (NCB) can be retained via an NCB Reserving Letter and transferred to a new car purchased within 3 years.

### Clause 12.6: Water Ingression and Hydrostatic Lock Damage
If a vehicle engine is stalled in floodwaters, attempting to crank or restart the engine causes hydrostatic lock, which is classified as consequential damage and excluded under base cover.

### Clause 12.7: Constructive Total Loss 75% IDV Rule
When the estimated repair and retrieval cost exceeds 75% of the vehicle's Insured Declared Value (IDV), the claim is settled on a Constructive Total Loss basis, paying out the full IDV.

### Clause 12.8: Compulsory Personal Accident Owner-Driver Exemption
An owner-driver is legally exempt from purchasing the mandatory ₹15 Lakhs CPA cover if they already hold an independent 24-hour personal accident policy with at least ₹15 Lakhs sum insured.

### Clause 12.9: Driving License Disqualification Impact
Operating an insured vehicle with an expired or invalid driving license, or under statutory intoxication (>30 mg alcohol/100 ml blood), voids all Own Damage and Third Party insurance cover.

### Clause 12.10: Surveyor Deputation for Losses Exceeding ₹50,000
Motor vehicle claims estimated above ₹50,000 must be physically surveyed and assessed by an independent IRDAI-licensed insurance surveyor before repairs begin.

---

## SECTION 13: GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL AND OMBUDSMAN FAQS

### Clause 13.1: Grievance Officer Escalation Timeline
An insurer's Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) must resolve written policyholder complaints within 14 calendar days of receipt. ### Clause 13.2: Approaching the Insurance Ombudsman
A complainant can approach the Insurance Ombudsman only after the insurer has rejected the complaint, provided an unsatisfactory response, or failed to reply within 30 days.

### Clause 13.3: Ombudsman Monetary Limit ₹30 Lakhs
The Insurance Ombudsman has legal jurisdiction to adjudicate insurance disputes where the total claim amount plus compensation sought does not exceed ₹30,00,000. ### Clause 13.4: One-Year Limitation for Ombudsman Complaints
A complaint to the Insurance Ombudsman must be lodged within 1 year from the date on which the insurer issued its written rejection or final decision.

### Clause 13.5: Penal Interest on Delayed Claims
If an insurer delays claim disbursement beyond 30 days of receiving the final required document, the insurer must pay penal interest at 2% above the prevailing RBI Bank Rate.

### Clause 13.6: Binding Nature of Ombudsman Decision
The Ombudsman's award is legally binding on the insurance company within 30 days of acceptance by the policyholder, but does not prevent the policyholder from moving Consumer Courts if dissatisfied.

# IRDAI POLICYHOLDER PROTECTION AND GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL GUIDELINES

**Regulatory Authority:** Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)  
**Regulation Title:** IRDAI (Protection of Policyholders' Interests and Allied Operations) Regulations, 2024  
**Document Reference:** IRDAI/REG/PPHI/2024/03  
**Applicability:** All General, Life, and Health Insurance Companies operating in India  

---

## SECTION 1: POINT OF SALE AND POLICY ISSUANCE STANDARDS

### Clause 1.1: Free-Look Cancellation Period
A policyholder of a personal health or life insurance policy is entitled to a Free-Look Period of 15 days from the date of receipt of the physical policy document (or 30 days in case of policies obtained through distance marketing or electronic modes) to review the terms and conditions.

If the insured disagrees with any clause, they may return the policy stating the reasons, upon which the insurer must refund the premium paid after deducting proportionate risk premium for the period on cover, medical examination expenses incurred by the insurer, and stamp duty charges.

### Clause 1.2: Minimum Grace Period Standards
Every individual life and health insurance policy shall provide a Grace Period of:
1.
30 days for policies with annual, half-yearly, or quarterly premium payment modes.
15 days for policies with monthly premium payment frequency.

During the grace period, coverage remains valid, and the insurer cannot deny an admissible claim. If a claim arises during the grace period, the overdue installment premium may be deducted from the claim settlement amount.

### Clause 1.3: Prohibition of Unilateral Mid-Term Alteration
An insurer shall not alter the terms, conditions, premium rates, or exclusions of an insurance policy during the subsistence of the policy term, except where permitted under specific IRDAI guidelines or statutory tax modifications.

### Clause 1.4: Policy Portability Rights
Every health insurance policyholder has the statutory right to port their individual or family floater health policy from one insurer to another at renewal.
The porting application must be submitted to the new insurer at least 45 days prior to the policy expiry date.

The acquiring insurer must credit accrued continuity benefits including waiting periods for pre-existing diseases and cumulative bonuses up to the sum insured of the previous policy.

---

## SECTION 2: CLAIMS PROCESSING AND SETTLEMENT TIMELINES

### Clause 2.1: Initial Query on Claim Documentation
An insurer shall raise all queries or requests for supplementary documentation related to a claim in a single communication within 15 days of receiving the initial claim intimation.
Piezomeal or staggered document requests are strictly prohibited under IRDAI regulations.

### Clause 2.2: Mandatory Claim Turnaround Time (TAT)
The insurer shall adjudicate, settle, or reject a claim within 30 days from the date of receipt of the final required document or surveyor's report. ### Clause 2.3: Special Investigation in Suspicious Claims
Where the circumstances of a claim warrant an in-depth investigation for suspected misrepresentation or fraud, the insurer shall initiate the investigation immediately and conclude it within 30 days.
The ultimate decision on claim settlement must not exceed 45 days from the date of original receipt of claim documents.

### Clause 2.4: Statutory Interest on Delayed Claim Payment
In the event of a delay in the payment of an admissible claim beyond the 30-day timeline mandated in Clause 2.2, the insurer shall be liable to pay penal interest to the policyholder at a rate 2% above the prevailing Reserve Bank of India (RBI) Bank Rate from the date of receipt of the last document until the actual date of payment.

---

## SECTION 3: GRIEVANCE REDRESSAL MECHANISM AND OMBUDSMAN JURISDICTION

### Clause 3.1: Insurer Internal Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO)
Every insurance company must designate a Chief Grievance Redressal Officer (GRO) at its head office and branch grievance officers at each operating branch.
A policyholder grievance submitted in writing or by email must be acknowledged within 3 business days and resolved with a reasoned written order within 14 calendar days of receipt.

### Clause 3.2: IRDAI Bima Bharosa Portal (Formerly IGMS)
If a policyholder does not receive a response from the insurer's GRO within 14 days, or is dissatisfied with the insurer's resolution, the policyholder may escalate the complaint to the IRDAI through the 'Bima Bharosa' online portal (toll-free: 155255 / 1800 4254 732).

### Clause 3.3: Eligibility and Jurisdiction of Insurance Ombudsman
A policyholder may approach the Insurance Ombudsman having territorial jurisdiction if:
1.
The grievance was first rejected by the insurer, or no resolution was provided within 30 days of submission to the GRO.
The total claim value, including compensation sought, does not exceed ₹30,00,000 (Rupees Thirty Lakhs).
The complaint is filed before the Ombudsman within one year from the date of receipt of the insurer's rejection order.
No complaint on the same matter is pending before any court of law, consumer commission, or arbitrator.

### Clause 3.4: Binding Nature of Ombudsman Award
An award passed by the Insurance Ombudsman is binding on the insurance company.
The insurer must comply with the award within 30 days of receiving the policyholder's letter of acceptance.
However, if the policyholder is dissatisfied with the Ombudsman's award, they retain the full legal right to approach Consumer Courts (DCDRC, SCDRC, NCDRC) or civil courts.

# IRDAI MASTER CIRCULAR ON HEALTH AND GENERAL INSURANCE OPERATIONS (2024)

**Issuing Authority:** Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI)  
**Circular Reference:** IRDAI/HLT/CIR/2024/08  
**Applicability:** All General and Standalone Health Insurers  

---

## SECTION 14: CASHLESS EVERYWHERE INITIATIVE & DISCHARGE TIMELINES

### Clause 14.1: Cashless Everywhere Nationwide Mandate
Every health insurer must provide cashless hospitalization facility to policyholders even at non-network hospitals, provided the hospital has at least 15 functional in-patient beds and agrees to the insurer's standard medical pricing tariff.

### Clause 14.2: One-Hour Pre-Authorization Timeline
The insurer or Third Party Administrator (TPA) must communicate its approval or query for cashless pre-authorization within 1 hour of receiving the request from the hospital. ### Clause 14.3: Three-Hour Final Discharge Clearance Mandate
Upon receiving the final hospital bill and discharge summary, the insurer or TPA must grant final authorization and clear the claim within 3 hours. Any hospital retention charges caused by insurer delay exceeding 3 hours must be borne solely by the insurer.

### Clause 14.4: Senior Citizen Priority Claims Desk
All insurers must maintain a dedicated senior citizen customer care desk and ensure that claims lodged by insured persons aged 60 and above are processed by priority adjusters within 15 days.

---

## SECTION 15: MOTOR CLAIMS SETTLEMENT AND SALVAGE RULES

### Clause 15.1: Cashless Garage Network Everywhere
For motor accidental claims, insurers must establish tie-ups with authorized and multi-brand workshops ensuring direct cashless settlement of admissible repair costs less deductibles.

### Clause 15.2: 48-Hour Surveyor Inspection Mandate
Upon receiving accidental motor claim intimation, an independent surveyor must physically inspect the vehicle within 48 hours in metro cities and 72 hours in non-metro areas.

### Clause 15.3: Fast-Track Assessment for Minor Losses
Accidental Own Damage claims with estimated damage below ₹20,000 may be processed on self-declaration and video survey without deputing a licensed physical surveyor.

### Clause 15.4: Salvage Value Realization on Total Loss
In total loss and constructive total loss (CTL) settlements under Clause 1.4, the salvage of the damaged vehicle can be retained by the insured with a mutually agreed deduction from the IDV payout, or surrendered to the insurer.

---

## SECTION 16: POLICYHOLDER PROTECTION AND DIGITAL REGULATORY COMPLIANCE

### Clause 16.1: Direct Bank Transfer for Free-Look Refunds
Refunds resulting from free-look cancellations under Clause 1.1 must be credited electronically via NEFT/RTGS to the policyholder's registered bank account within 7 business days.

### Clause 16.2: Prohibition of Mid-Term Cancellation by Insurer
An insurer cannot cancel an active health insurance policy during the policy year on grounds of multiple claims or adverse claims experience.

### Clause 16.3: Digital ABHA and e-Insurance Account Integration
All policyholders are entitled to store and view their health and general insurance contracts in electronic form through authorized Insurance Repositories linked to their Ayushman Bharat Health Account (ABHA).

### Clause 16.4: Zero Deductions on Electronic Hospitalization Records
Where cashless claims are verified electronically through the National Health Claims Exchange (NHCX), no administrative handling fees or documentation charges may be levied on the insured.

# SECUREDRIVE PRIVATE CAR COMPREHENSIVE PACKAGE POLICY

**Product Name:** SecureDrive Private Car Comprehensive Package Policy  
**Product UIN:** IRDAI/NL-GI/SD-PC/V.2/2024-25  
**Regulating Authority:** Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India (IRDAI) / Indian Motor Tariff (IMT)  
**Document Type:** Standard Private Car Package Policy Terms and Conditions  

---

## SECTION 1: LOSS OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE INSURED (OWN DAMAGE)

### Clause 1.1: Scope of Own Damage Cover
The Insurer will indemnify the Insured against loss or damage to the private vehicle insured and its accessories whilst thereon by:
1.
Fire, explosion, self-ignition, or lightning.
Burglary, housebreaking, or theft.
Riot and strike.
Earthquake (fire and shock damage).
Flood, typhoon, hurricane, storm, tempest, inundation, cyclone, hailstorm, and frost.
Accidental external means.
Malicious act.
Terrorist activity.
Whilst in transit by road, rail, inland waterway, lift, elevator, or air.
Landslide and rockslide.

### Clause 1.2: Depreciation Scale on Parts for Partial Loss Claims
In the settlement of claims for accidental partial loss, depreciation shall be deducted on parts replaced at the following rates:
1.
Rubber, nylon, plastic parts, tyres, tubes, batteries, and airbags: 50% depreciation.
Fiberglass components: 30% depreciation.
All parts made of glass: Nil (0% depreciation).

All other parts made of steel/metal:
   - Vehicle age up to 6 months: Nil depreciation.
   - Vehicle age > 6 months up to 1 year: 5% depreciation.
   - Vehicle age > 1 year up to 2 years: 10% depreciation.
   - Vehicle age > 2 years up to 3 years: 15% depreciation.
   - Vehicle age > 3 years up to 4 years: 25% depreciation.
   - Vehicle age > 4 years up to 5 years: 35% depreciation.
   - Vehicle age > 5 years up to 10 years: 40% depreciation.
   - Vehicle age over 10 years: 50% depreciation.

### Clause 1.3: Insured Declared Value (IDV) Definition
The Insured Declared Value (IDV) of the vehicle shall be treated as the 'Sum Insured' for the purpose of this policy. The IDV is fixed at the commencement of each policy period for the insured vehicle on the basis of the manufacturer's listed selling price less depreciation based on vehicle age.

### Clause 1.4: Total Loss and Constructive Total Loss (CTL)
A vehicle will be considered to be a Constructive Total Loss (CTL) where the aggregate cost of retrieval and/or repair of the vehicle, subject to terms and conditions of the policy, exceeds 75% of the Insured Declared Value (IDV) of the vehicle. In the event of Total Loss or CTL, the Insurer pays the full IDV after surrendering vehicle salvage and registration papers.

### Clause 1.5: Towing and Protection Expenses
If the insured vehicle is disabled by reason of accidental damage, the Insurer will bear the reasonable cost of protection and removal to the nearest repairer up to a maximum limit of ₹1,500 for private cars. Any additional towing charges must be borne by the Insured unless the Roadside Assistance add-on was purchased.

---

## SECTION 2: LIABILITY TO THIRD PARTIES

### Clause 2.1: Third Party Bodily Injury or Death Cover
Subject to the limits of liability, the Insurer will indemnify the Insured in the event of an accident caused by or arising out of the use of the vehicle against all sums including claimant's costs and expenses which the Insured shall become legally liable to pay in respect of death of or bodily injury to any third party person. In accordance with Motor Vehicles Act, liability for bodily injury or death is unlimited.

### Clause 2.2: Third Party Property Damage (TPPD) Limit
The Insurer indemnifies damage to property belonging to any third party person up to a maximum statutory limit of ₹7,50,000 in respect of any one accident or series of accidents arising out of one event. The Policyholder may opt for a restricted TPPD limit of ₹6,000 to obtain a minor premium discount.

### Clause 2.3: Legal Expenses in Third Party Claims
The Insurer will pay all reasonable legal costs and expenses incurred with its prior written consent in defending any suit or criminal prosecution brought against the Insured or the Authorized Driver in connection with an accident.

---

## SECTION 3: COMPULSORY PERSONAL ACCIDENT COVER FOR OWNER-DRIVER

### Clause 3.1: Compulsory Personal Accident (CPA) Scope
The Insurer undertakes to pay compensation up to a Capital Sum Insured of ₹15,00,000 for bodily injury or death sustained by the Owner-Driver of the vehicle in direct connection with the insured vehicle whilst driving, mounting into, or dismounting from the vehicle.

### Clause 3.2: CPA Scale of Compensation
Compensation under CPA is payable as follows:
1.
Death: 100% of Capital Sum Insured (₹15,00,000).
Loss of two limbs or sight of two eyes: 100% of Capital Sum Insured (₹15,00,000).
Loss of one limb or sight of one eye: 50% of Capital Sum Insured (₹7,50,000).
Permanent total disablement from injuries: 100% of Capital Sum Insured (₹15,00,000).

### Clause 3.3: Exemption from CPA Cover
An owner-driver may opt out of the Compulsory Personal Accident cover if they already possess an effective standalone 24-hour Personal Accident cover with Sum Insured of at least ₹15,00,000, or own another vehicle with valid CPA cover.

---

## SECTION 4: DEDUCTIBLES AND DISCOUNTS

### Clause 4.1: Compulsory Deductible
The Insurer shall not be liable for each and every claim arising under Section 1 (Own Damage) in respect of the compulsory deductible:
- For private cars with engine capacity not exceeding 1,500 cc: ₹1,000 per claim.
- For private cars with engine capacity exceeding 1,500 cc: ₹2,000 per claim. ### Clause 4.2: Voluntary Deductible
If the Insured opts for an additional Voluntary Deductible at policy issuance, the Insured shall bear that amount on each claim in addition to the Compulsory Deductible, in exchange for a premium discount on the basic Own Damage premium:
- Voluntary Deductible ₹2,500: 20% discount on OD premium (max ₹750).
- Voluntary Deductible ₹5,000: 25% discount on OD premium (max ₹1,500).
- Voluntary Deductible ₹7,500: 30% discount on OD premium (max ₹2,000).
- Voluntary Deductible ₹15,000: 35% discount on OD premium (max ₹2,500).

### Clause 4.3: No Claim Bonus (NCB) Scale
No Claim Bonus (NCB) is earned on the Own Damage premium for every claim-free year according to the following progressive scale:
- 1 claim-free year: 20% discount.
- 2 consecutive claim-free years: 25% discount.
- 3 consecutive claim-free years: 35% discount.
- 4 consecutive claim-free years: 45% discount.
- 5 consecutive claim-free years: 50% maximum discount. If a claim is lodged during the policy period, the NCB is reduced to Nil (0%) at the subsequent renewal, unless a Zero NCB Protection add-on was in effect. ### Clause 4.4: Transfer of No Claim Bonus
NCB belongs to the Insured (vehicle owner) and not to the vehicle. Upon sale of the insured vehicle, the Insured can retain the NCB certificate and apply the earned discount to a replacement vehicle purchased within 3 years.

---

## SECTION 5: GENERAL EXCLUSIONS APPLICABLE TO ALL SECTIONS

### Clause 5.1: Contractual Liability Exclusion
The policy does not cover any liability arising out of an agreement or contract entered into by the Insured which would not have attached in the absence of such contract.

### Clause 5.2: Consequential Loss and Depreciation
The Insurer is not liable for any consequential financial loss, depreciation, wear and tear, or mechanical or electrical breakdown, failure, or breakage.

### Clause 5.3: Driving Under the Influence (DUI)
The Insurer shall not be liable for any accidental loss, damage, or third-party liability caused whilst the vehicle is being driven by any person under the influence of intoxicating liquor or drugs.
A blood alcohol content exceeding 30 mg per 100 ml of blood constitutes statutory intoxication.

### Clause 5.4: Driving Without Valid Driving License
The Insurer is not liable if the vehicle is being driven by any person who is not holding an effective and valid driving license at the time of the accident, or by a person disqualified from holding or obtaining such a license.

### Clause 5.5: Geographic and War Limitations
Any accidental loss or damage occurring outside the geographical boundaries of India is excluded, unless specifically extended by endorsement to Nepal, Bhutan, Bangladesh, or Sri Lanka.
Loss due to war, invasion, or nuclear weapons is excluded.

### Clause 5.6: Speed Contests and Motor Rallies
Any loss, damage, or liability incurred whilst the insured vehicle is used for racing, pacemaking, speed testing, reliability trials, or motor rallies is excluded.

### Clause 5.7: Hydrostatic Lock and Engine Inundation
Damage caused to the engine of the vehicle due to water ingression or hydrostatic lock caused by attempting to restart an inundated vehicle is excluded under base cover, unless an Engine Protector add-on is active.

---

## SECTION 6: CLAIMS SETTLEMENT AND INTIMATION RULES

### Clause 6.1: Notice of Accidental Loss
Notice shall be given in writing to the Insurer immediately upon the occurrence of any accidental loss or damage, and in the event of any claim, within 48 to 72 hours of the incident.

### Clause 6.2: Theft and Burglary Procedure
In the event of theft or criminal act, immediate notice must be given to the local Police authorities and a First Information Report (FIR) must be registered.
A final untraced report (Non-Traceable Certificate) certified by the judicial magistrate must be submitted to the Insurer before a total theft claim can be settled.

### Clause 6.3: Independent Surveyor Appointment
For any Own Damage claim where the estimated loss exceeds ₹50,000, an IRDAI-licensed independent insurance surveyor must be deputed to inspect the vehicle before dismantling and repairs commence.

### Clause 6.4: Cashless Workshop Settlement
Under the Cashless garage network, the Insurer directly settles approved repair costs with the authorized workshop, less the applicable depreciation (Clause 1.2), compulsory deductible (Clause 4.1), and salvage value.

## SECTION 7: HEALTH POLICY DAY CARE PROCEDURES (ANNEXURE I)

### Clause 7.1: Microsurgical Eye Operations
Covers day-care cataract surgery, vitrectomy, trabeculectomy, retinal detachment surgery, and corneal surgery with laser treatment completed under 24 hours.

### Clause 7.2: ENT Surgical Procedures
Covers myringotomy, tympanoplasty, stapedectomy, mastoidectomy, turbinectomy, nasal polypectomy, and tonsillectomy performed under local or general anesthesia.

### Clause 7.3: Oncology Day Care Procedures
Covers outpatient and daycare intravenous chemotherapy, radiotherapy (including intensity-modulated radiation therapy and cyberknife), and brachytherapy.

### Clause 7.4: Urology and Nephrology Procedures
Covers lithotripsy (ESWL) for kidney stones, transurethral resection of the prostate (TURP), ureteroscopy (URS), and dialysis for acute renal failure.

### Clause 7.5: Orthopedic and Joint Day Care Interventions
Covers closed reduction of fractures, arthroscopic meniscus repair, carpal tunnel decompression, and removal of internal orthopedic fixation devices.

### Clause 7.6: Gastroenterology Day Care Interventions
Covers therapeutic endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), endoscopic sclerotherapy for variceal bleeding, and polypectomy of colon.

---

## SECTION 8: HEALTH POLICY CRITICAL ILLNESS SPECIFICATIONS (ANNEXURE II)

### Clause 8.1: Cancer of Specified Severity
Covers malignant tumor characterized by the uncontrolled growth and spread of malignant cells with invasion and destruction of normal tissue, confirmed by histological biopsy.

### Clause 8.2: Myocardial Infarction (First Heart Attack)
Covers the death of a portion of the heart muscle arising from inadequate blood supply, evidenced by elevated cardiac enzymes (Troponin T/I) and new characteristic ECG changes.

### Clause 8.3: Open Heart Replacement or Repair of Heart Valves
Covers the actual undergoing of open-heart surgery to replace or repair one or more heart valves as certified by an independent cardiologist.

### Clause 8.4: Kidney Failure Requiring Regular Dialysis
Covers end-stage renal disease presenting as chronic irreversible failure of both kidneys to function, necessitating regular peritoneal or hemodialysis.

### Clause 8.5: Major Organ and Bone Marrow Transplant
Covers the actual undergoing of a transplant as a recipient for heart, lung, liver, kidney, pancreas, or human bone marrow using hematopoietic stem cells.

### Clause 8.6: Stroke Resulting in Permanent Symptoms
Covers any cerebrovascular incident producing neurological sequelae lasting at least 3 months, confirmed by modern neuro-imaging (MRI or CT scan).

---

## SECTION 9: MOTOR POLICY ADD-ON ENDORSEMENTS (SCHEDULE M)

### Clause 9.1: Zero Depreciation (Bumper to Bumper) Cover
In the event of an admissible claim under Section 1 (Own Damage), no depreciation deduction specified in Clause 1.2 will be applied to replaced parts including rubber, nylon, plastic, and fiberglass.

### Clause 9.2: Engine and Gearbox Protector Add-on
Covers repair or replacement of internal engine parts, gearbox components, differential, and power steering pump damaged solely by water ingression (hydrostatic lock) or lubricating oil leakage.

### Clause 9.3: Return to Invoice (RTI) Cover
In the event of Total Loss, Constructive Total Loss (Clause 1.4), or Theft (Clause 6.2), the Insurer will pay the difference between the Insured Declared Value (IDV) and the original on-road purchase price of the vehicle including registration and road tax.

### Clause 9.4: Consumables Expense Cover
Covers costs of consumables damaged or depleted in an accident, including engine oil, gearbox oil, brake fluid, coolant, AC refrigerant gas, nuts, bolts, washers, and oil filter.

### Clause 9.5: Roadside Assistance (RSA) Emergency Cover
Provides 24x7 roadside assistance services including flat tyre change, battery jumpstart, emergency fuel delivery (up to 5 litres), minor on-site mechanical repairs, and towing to nearest network garage up to 50 km.

### Clause 9.6: Key and Lock Replacement Cover
Reimburses the cost of replacing stolen or lost vehicle keys, including recoding of electronic vehicle immobilizer system and replacement of lock assembly up to ₹25,000 per policy year.

### Clause 9.7: Daily Commute / Loss of Use Allowance
Pays a daily fixed cash allowance of ₹1,000 per day (up to maximum 10 days) to cover local travel expenses while the insured vehicle is undergoing accidental repairs in an authorized garage.

### Clause 9.8: Tyre and Rim Protection Cover
Covers accidental damage to tyres (bulges, bursts, cut repairs) and alloy wheel rims where the damage is not accompanied by damage to the insured vehicle itself.

## SECTION 10: IRDAI OMBUDSMAN JURISDICTION & POWERS (ANNEXURE R)

### Clause 10.1: Territorial Ombudsman Centers
Establishes 17 Insurance Ombudsman offices across India (including Mumbai, Delhi, Bengaluru, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad, Ahmedabad, and Chandigarh) having exclusive territorial jurisdiction based on insurer branch location.

### Clause 10.2: Types of Complaints Entertained by Ombudsman
The Ombudsman entertains complaints relating to: delay in claim settlement, partial or total repudiation of claims, disputes over premium paid or payable, non-issuance of policy documents, and mis-selling.

### Clause 10.3: Ex-Gratia and Compensation Awards
The Ombudsman has statutory power to grant compensation for financial loss as well as harassment and mental agony, subject to the overall ceiling of ₹30,00,000 specified in Clause 3.3.

### Clause 10.4: Insurer Compliance Verification
If an insurer fails to comply with an Ombudsman award within 30 days of receiving the complainant's acceptance letter, the IRDAI may initiate supervisory enforcement action including regulatory penalties under Section 102 of the Insurance Act.
